ns2:course.label: Res Sem in Consumer Behavior
ns2:course.description: Advanced doctoral level seminar which critically examines the relevance of behavioral and social constructs for generating consumer behavior theories. It specifically discusses the need for, and procedures with which to modify behavioral/social processes. 4 graduate hours. No professional credit. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 12 hours, if topics vary. Prerequisite: Ph.D. standing in BADM or consent of instructor.
